To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a CA can be used to model population, employment and their spatial distributions, and that the resulting model outperforms all other models in terms of accuracy of predictions and of fractal dimensions.

(i) the model is able to reproduce the observed spatial patterns in both population and employment, and the observed spatial distribution of land use; (ii) the model is also able to reproduce the correct spatial patterns in population and employment densities; and (iii) the model can be used to predict the spatial patterns of population, employment, and land use in both the Greater Dublin Region and Belgium.

the constrained CA framework, with its multiple activity-based variable-grid structure and its distance-decay transition rules, is capable of modelling the spatial dynamics of population, economic activities and land use at the same resolution and with a high level of accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated framework for the analysis of urban systems.
the development of a general framework for integrated spatial modelling of land use and population, which can be applied at a range of scales and to both urban-centred and polycentric systems.
the development of a general framework for the modelling of land use and the location of population and economic activities, and with its application to a number of real world cases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model performs well, is robust, and has the potential to be a useful tool for policy makers.
the model performs very well.
the model is a good one and that it is the best of its type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a constrained CA framework, with the appropriate spatial interaction functions, can model the location of activities, and hence of population, with good accuracy, at the scale of the entire urban system and its hinterland, and that this is true for both polycentric and urban-centred systems.

we have developed a new modelling framework that captures the spatial dynamics of land use and activity at multiple scales, and we have shown that it is capable of producing accurate predictions for a variety of spatially explicit variables.
we have developed a model that can be applied to any region of any size and shape, with any number of land uses and activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CA model with a single transition rule can be applied successfully to both urban and rural regions.

it is possible to model the entire urban system in a single framework, with a spatial resolution that is fine enough to capture the spatial dynamics of urban systems, and to do so with a single model that is parsimonious in terms of the number of parameters required to fit the data.
the spatial dynamics of land use are best captured when the spatial dynamics of activities are also included in the same model.
